absent: Policy allocation and release, thread creation, rate limit update, fast switch enablement, domain rebuild, governor attribute set handling, and update hook add and remove internals are not shown.
Per policy versus global tunables selection rule, tunables layout, rate limit units, and sysfs type behavior are not shown.
Update path frequency selection, caching, work queueing, interrupt work handling, and limits changed consumption are not shown.
Priority conversion, priority ceiling value, CPU count and active mask maintenance, runqueue priority set and cleanup, and fitness predicate definition are not shown.

Scheduling clock, tick length, usage bucket enumeration, group accounting, runqueue and task layout, virtual time enablement, sequence counter layout, steal clock source, and sleep time caller contract are not shown.

findings.text: The schedutil governor publishes a frequency governor identity with dynamic switching behavior and lifecycle operations for initialization, teardown, activation, deactivation and limit handling.
A default governor accessor yields the schedutil governor instance, and a predicate reports whether a given policy currently uses that governor.

Initialization rejects a policy that already holds governor data, enables fast switching, allocates policy state and creates its thread, then either attaches to existing global tunables or allocates fresh tunables seeded from the policy transition delay and registers them, rebuilding scheduling domains on success and unwinding thread, allocation, registration and fast switching on failure.

Teardown drops the tunables reference, clears policy association and possibly the shared global entry, then stops the thread, frees policy state, disables fast switching and rebuilds scheduling domains.

Activation resets frequency tracking state, records whether limit updates are required, chooses a shared policy updater or a single policy performance or frequency updater based on sharing and driver capability, clears per CPU records and only then publishes update hooks; deactivation removes hooks from every policy CPU, waits for read side grace, and for the slow path synchronizes interrupt work and cancels thread work.
A global tunables mutex serializes inspection and installation of shared versus per policy tunables, reference acquisition and release, governor data assignment and clearing of the shared pointer.

Limit application in the slow path holds the policy work mutex, while thread teardown flushes pending work, stops the thread and destroys the mutex and is skipped entirely when fast switching is active.
Priority to CPU tracking uses a per priority vector pairing a count with a CPU mask, and a top container holding one such vector per priority level plus a per CPU current priority mapping.
Priority bookkeeping defines a level count equal to maximum real time priority plus one, with invalid marker negative one, normal marker zero, and higher marker one hundred.

Lookup entry points expose a plain search and a fitness filtered search; the filtered search walks priorities below the task priority, applies an optional capacity predicate to the candidate mask, continues when no candidate survives, and falls back to an unfiltered search to prefer priority over fit.

Candidate inspection reads the vector count first, issues a read barrier, then reads the mask, treating empty counts, lack of affinity overlap, masking by active set, or an emptied result as no match at that level.
A dedicated enable operation turns on interrupt time accounting through a static branch, backed by per CPU interrupt time state.
Interrupt time attribution accumulates a delta into a chosen usage counter and a running total plus a conditional tick remainder while holding a per CPU sequence protected update section.

Interrupt exit accounting measures elapsed time since entry, advances the entry stamp, derives nesting depth adjusted by an offset, ignores disabled configurations, and attributes hard interrupt versus soft interrupt time while leaving soft interrupt time occurring in its dedicated thread with that thread.

User, guest and indexed system accounting each advance process and group counters and a selected usage bucket, with guest also advancing a guest specific field, nice tasks using nice buckets, and system dispatch selecting guest for virtual CPU tasks outside interrupt context, interrupt or soft interrupt buckets inside those contexts, and plain system otherwise.

Steal accounting adds to the steal bucket; idle accounting adds to input wait versus idle based on waiters; the native steal clock yields zero; paravirt steal handling clamps observed growth to a supplied maximum, accounts it and advances the prior stamp.

Tick other time handling assumes interrupts disabled and consumes up to a maximum first from steal then from pending interrupt tick remainder, where one configuration drains a bounded tick remainder and an alternate configuration always yields zero.
Execution sum observation has two forms, one reading directly and another reading while holding the task runqueue lock pair.

Thread group time refreshes the current task runtime when in the same group, then under read copy update protection and the signal statistics lock sums signal level totals with per thread user, system and execution sums.

Task time observation returns stored values directly when virtual time is off, otherwise retries under a sequence guard and adds pending virtual time to system or user according to current state while skipping sleeping states; elapsed virtual time clamps backward clock movement to zero.

Process tick accounting in one configuration subtracts steal plus interrupt time from the tick total and drops fully covered ticks, otherwise routes dedicated soft interrupt thread ticks to soft interrupt, user ticks to user, idle task ticks to idle, virtual CPU ticks to guest and remainder to system, while an alternate configuration performs no action.

Idle and dynamic tick transitions maintain entry time, elapsed flag and per wait state steal adjustments under a sleep time sequence lock, starting and stopping idle windows on tick stop and start and on interrupt entry and exit subject to generic virtual time and interrupt time enablement.

Idle and wait field reads in one configuration retry under the sleep sequence and optionally add live elapsed time net of pending steal, while an alternate configuration returns the stored slot; public idle and wait accessors supply current time and a wait based delta flag, and a sleep time helper selects generic versus dynamic tick source, scales to microseconds and optionally reports update time.

Publishing update hooks before per CPU records are ready would let a shared policy updater observe uninitialized sibling state, and missing the ordered barrier between limit flag and limit values could lose a limit change; failure unwinding must reverse registration, global pointer, thread and fast switch steps.

Priority mask reads are intentionally racy with concurrent empties and rely on barriers plus higher level pull or retry behavior rather than locking, and idle field readers must tolerate concurrent steal adjusted updates via sequence retry.
